text:
Sam: Thanks everyone — quick follow-ups from the infra update. A few things we promised to clarify:

Claire: Can you confirm which regions get pre-warmed GPUs vs on-demand bursting?

Jin (infra): EMEA + us-west get pre-warm pools initially. APAC starts on-demand with warm-up windows; we're targeting APAC pre-warm in Q3.

Maria: What's the exact fallback order when a region runs out? Is it region -> tier -> model variant?

Jin (infra): Fallback order is: 1) same region, lower-cost instance (burst fallback), 2) neighbor region within latency SLO (routing), 3) compatible quantized variant in any region. We will publish the policy JSON and examples soon.

Leo: @Jin when you say 'neighbor region' does that include cross-cloud? We have customers in GCP-only accounts.

Jin (infra): Good question. Cross-cloud routing is disabled by default for Private deployments and customers with strict network policies. Hosted accounts may opt-in. We'll add a config flag doc.

Ava (sre-oncall): For oncall: if autoscaler spikes, will alerts fire per-pool or per-region? Want to avoid pager fatigue.

Ravi (eng-sre): Alerts are per-pool for throughput/queue. We only escalate to paging if the queue is >75% and persists for >3 minutes and automatic fallback hasn't recovered capacity. We'll add thresholds to the runbook.

Sam: Action items: Jin to PR fallback docs + a sample config snippet, Ravi to update oncall runbook with exact thresholds, Claire to share the region pre-warm schedule. Timeline: EOD Thu for docs, next Tue for runbook.

Maria: Small ask — can we get a sample `autoscaler.policy` snippet for devs to test locally?

Jin (infra): Yup, here's a minimal example you can drop into a dev cluster:
```
autoscaler:
  policy: region-prefer
  fallthrough:
    - type: cheaper-instance
    - type: neighbor-region
      max_latency_ms: 120
    - type: quantized-variant
```

Claire: I will circulate the Gantt for pre-warm windows after I sync with procurement and cloud partners.

Sam: Thanks all, closing the loop here. :thumbsup:
